title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: A student asks the woodshop assistant, "Is the CNC router free Tuesday morning?" The assistant has a tool get_schedule(machine, date) and calls it, getting back "booked 9-11am." At the moment the assistant writes its final answer, which of these actually counts as part of this turn's context window?

options.text: The complete woodshop safety manual, in case training comes up
Every future booking request any student might make
The get_schedule tool's definition and the result it returned
The full maintenance history of the CNC router, since it could be relevant

items.stem: A student's session unfolds in three steps: step 1 checks router availability, step 2 checks the student's safety-training status, step 3 gives a final answer combining both. At step 3, the assistant wants to mention the router's step-1 availability in its answer. Does it need to call get_schedule again to do that?

options.text: Yes, because tool results expire after one step
No, step 1's result is still sitting in context from earlier in the same session
Yes, because context is cleared between tool calls
No, but only if the student repeats the question

items.stem: A student who completed safety training during yesterday's session returns today, in a brand-new session, and asks the assistant to confirm it's on file. In one sentence, why might the assistant not know, even though it was already discussed yesterday?

A woodworking club's assistant has been running one long session all afternoon, with dozens of unrelated small-talk turns piling up. A student now asks a safety question. The context window isn't full yet. What's the likely risk of all that leftover small talk?

options.text: The model will automatically summarize the old turns to protect accuracy
None — more context in the window always helps the model answer
The request will fail outright before the model generates anything
Accuracy may degrade, since irrelevant tokens compete with the few that matter

items.stem: The woodshop's table-saw manual is 80 pages long. In one or two sentences, how should the assistant use retrieval to answer a question about blade replacement, rather than loading the whole manual into its prompt?
